Megaspeed to cooperate with U.S. probe into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang scandal
 Megaspeed, in a statement on November 12, said that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously
 Updated - November 12, 2026 04:51 pm IST - Hong Kong 
 AP READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 A screengrab from CTI video footage obtained November 9, 2026 shows Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a woman identified by Reuters as Alice Huang (in pink dress) after comparison with a photograph obtained separately, attending a dinner at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan May 22, 2025.
 | Photo Credit: Reuters
 Megaspeed, the Singapore-headquartered tech company at the centre of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's scandal, pledged on Thursday (November 12, 2026) to cooperate with investigations into concerns over risks to U.S. national security.
 Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded In its first statement since Mr. Huang admitted to having an affair with a Chinese woman and former executive of the company, Megaspeed said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.”
 “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government.”
 Nvidia's board of directors was reported to be meeting to discuss Mr. Huang's situation, but there was no word on any outcome from those discussions.
